evidence: books/store-log-programs.lisp:234-236: `(defun fn-lg-recover-tail (ks extent) ... (mv (fn-lgk-frontier ks) (nfix (- (nfix extent) (fn-lgk-frontier ks)))))`; host/native/io.lisp:6716-6717: `(destructuring-bind (offset count) (fnn-call 'fn-lg-recover-tail ks extent) (fnn-log-pwrite fd offset (fnn-make-octets count))`. Extents double: books/store-log-extend.lisp:63 `(max (max (* 2 (nfix extent)) (* unit (ceiling need unit))) unit)`.
fix: Have ACL2 answer the zeroing as a bounded sequence of ranges (for example fn-lg-recover-tail-step returning the next (offset count) with count capped at a work quantum) and write from one reusable zero buffer. Or skip the zeroing entirely when the probe verdict is :complete with zero debris, since the tail is then already zeros. Wrap the post-stream steps in unwind-protect so FD is closed on failure.
reviewer: In io.lisp:6716-6717, fnn-log-recover calls fnn-log-pwrite with (fnn-make-octets count), and count is extent minus frontier (store-log-programs.lisp:234-236). That is one allocation the size of the whole tail on every recover. All three open paths call it (io.lisp:7513, 7923, 8179). The probe also runs on every segment stream (io.lisp:6654) and walks every unit from the stop to the extent with one pread per stride (6556-6561). The FD leak is real too: only the stream is inside the handler-case that closes fd (6705-6713), and the pwrite/fdatasync after it are not. Whether the tail actually reaches GiB depends on how the extent doubling meets the rotation policy. I could not confirm that by reading, but the mechanism is as described.
scenario: The active segment grew by doubling to 8 GiB, because publications were deferred or K is large and records are big, and its frontier is at 4.1 GiB. Every writable open, including a clean restart, then allocates a 3.9 GiB zero array (fnn-make-octets) and rewrites 3.9 GiB of zeros that are already zeros. Restarts become slow, and they fail with heap exhaustion once the slack exceeds dynamic space, so a node that ran fine cannot reopen. The same tail is also probed unit by unit (fnn-log-probe-tail) on every open, which is O(extent/unit) preads. A failure in this pwrite or fdatasync also leaks FD, because only the stream step is wrapped in the closing handler-case (io.lisp:6705-6713).
title: Recovery zeroes the whole tail [F, extent) with one in-memory buffer of that size, on every writable open
